results.title: Malcolm
results.brief_description: Cascade Films’ Malcolm (1986) follows a shy man (Colin Friels) with a genius for invention. After being sacked from the tram depot for building his own locomotive, he meets Judy (Lindy Davies) and Frank (John Hargreaves), two would-be bank robbers.

constellations_primary.name: Quirky, eccentric, charming
constellations_primary.description: The eponymous character of Malcolm (1986) is a kind and gentle young man obsessed with trams and making gadgets. Such charming and eccentric figures have a long lineage in screen history.

results.description:
In 1986, the same year that Crocodile Dundee stormed the US box office, a much quirkier film was also making international waves. Cascade Films’ Malcolm (1986) follows a shy man (Colin Friels) with a genius for invention. After being sacked from the tram depot for building his own locomotive, he meets Judy (Lindy Davies) and Frank (John Hargreaves), two would-be bank robbers. The trio use Malcolm’s gadgets to pull off the heist of the century, forming an unlikely family in the process.

The first film from director/writer duo Nadia Tass and David Parker, Malcolm was followed by many more films by the pair, including Rikky and Pete (1988), The Big Steal (1990), and Amy (1997).

Malcolm won eight AFI awards and received international acclaim.

results.title: Immersive Sound in Cinema
results.brief_description:
When Star Wars hit cinemas in the late 1970s and 80s, sound engineer Tomlinson Holman noticed a problem: the rich, detailed audio created during production wasn’t being heard properly in theatres. His solution was THX – a new sound standard that ensured films played exactly as filmmakers intended.
When Return of the Jedi (1983) premiered, only THX-certified cinemas could show it. Audiences were greeted by the now-iconic ‘Deep Note’ – a rising wave of tones swelling into a mighty D major chord. It shook the room and set the stage for the galaxy far, far away – as well as a new level of excellence in cinema sound.
Fun fact: THX was named after George Lucas’s first film, THX 1138 (1971).

results.title: Isopod
results.credit_line: Isopod (2025) transforms you into a tiny pill-bug navigating a huge Australian bush. You roll, zip, and slam through colourful leaves, twigs, and moss, using magnetic physics to stick, repel, and bounce. Team up with other bugs to solve puzzles, smash through obstacles, and outsmart dangerous fire-ants. Along the way, you uncover the rhythms of the ecosystem, watching plants grow, insects scuttle, and animals interact. The game blends playful, kinetic platforming with a gentle, immersive lesson in nature, showing how even the smallest creatures can make a big impact in their world.

results.title: Immersive sound in cinema
results.brief_description:
By the early 1950s, television was keeping people at home, and cinemas needed to offer something special. Sound became key to creating an experience that couldn’t be matched in the living room.
In 1952, This Is Cinerama wowed New York audiences with a huge curved screen and a new multi-channel sound system developed by Hazard E Reeves. Instead of a single speaker, Cinerama used seven – five behind the screen and two behind the audience – wrapping viewers in sound.
This early form of surround sound transformed movie-going, setting the stage for the immersive audio experiences we expect in cinemas today.

constellations_primary.name: Immersive sound: from THX to surround (a placeholder)
constellations_primary.description: The THX sound became a symbol of immersive cinema, signalling pristine audio quality. From Return of the Jedi to videogames, creators explored spatial sound, dynamic mixing, and atmospheric audio, showing how sound shapes experience, emotion, and perception across multiple media forms.

results.title: Celeste
results.brief_description: Celeste (2018) is a game about continuing onwards, even when things are tough. Created by Noel Berry and Maddy Thorson just before Thorson’s gender transition, the game is a metaphor for a young woman facing struggles with mental health and identity, represented as one great task: climbing a mountain.

constellations_primary.name: Keeping the pace
constellations_primary.description: Whether speedrunning or in slow motion, explore how running builds tension, emotion and excitement on screen.

results.description:
Celeste (2018) is a game about continuing onwards, even when things are tough. Created by Noel Berry and Maddy Thorson just before Thorson’s gender transition, the game is a metaphor for a young woman facing struggles with mental health and identity, represented as one great task: climbing a mountain.

The game’s precise movement and challenging levels have drawn a passionate community of players who race through the mountain in speedruns, sharing strategies and competing for the fastest climbs. Celeste celebrates persistence, reflection, and skill, showing how a game can tell a deeply personal story while connecting people through play.

results.title: Suzi's story
results.creator_credit: Iain Gillespie, Carlyon-Gillespie Production and Pro-image
results.brief_description: This is the true story of the Lovegrove family. It is the story of Suzi, a loving wife and mother stricken with AIDS. This documentary poignantly deals with this tragic and deadly virus, and seeks to educate the viewer about the debilitating effects of AIDS not only on the victim, but on those who love her. This film sensitively brings home the reality of AIDS. It won’t easily be forgotten.

results.title: Blackmagic Design Media Preservation Lab
results.brief_description: The Media Preservation Lab is a purposed built public facing lab.
results.description: There are about 250,000 artefacts in the ACMI Collection. We’ve been collecting film, videogames, artworks, home movies, stills and press kits – as well as a huge range of other paraphernalia – for over 75 years, ever since ACMI was conceived as a film lending and education organisation known as the State Film Centre. Inside the Blackmagic Media Preservation Lab, our staff and collaborators are digitising our film and time-based media collections, assessing physical artefacts from our videogame collection and film donations, as well as conducting hours of quality assessment work on our born-digital works to make the collection accessible onsite and online.
